questions: When duplicates exist, does 'remaining unique integers' mean we consider each occurrence separately (i.e., treat the list as a multiset) or do we deduplicate first and then repeat values as needed to fill the output length?
For the min/max selection, if multiple equal values qualify (e.g., multiple 5s when picking min), which one is removed? Does it matter which index is removed as long as one instance is removed?
Should the output list have the same length as the input list, or could it be shorter if we deduplicate?
Is the input list guaranteed to contain only integers, or could it have other numeric types (floats) or non-numeric values?
When picking min/max, do we consider the current remaining list as a whole, or do we consider only the set of distinct values remaining?
If the input list is empty, should the output be an empty list, or is that an error?
Does 'strange order' imply we must alternate min and max until exhaustion, or could we stop early if only one value remains?
If we deduplicate, and after deduplication we have an odd number of unique values, does the last step pick min or max?
